fields.meta_title: Document Automation Software You Build and Own | Emergent
fields.meta_description: Describe the files you send and receive. Emergent builds document automation that drafts quotes and letters and reads PDFs. Free to start.
fields.h1: Build Document Automation for What You Send and Receive
fields.hero_description: Describe the templates you fill by hand and the PDFs people send you. Emergent builds document automation that drafts from your data and reads every upload into fields.
fields.features_subheading: Start with the parts your first document needs. The rest are ready when a second document calls for them.
fields.feature_1:
Templates from the files you already use

Start from a Word or Google Docs file your team sends today. Fields fill where they sit in the text, and the line-item table grows to fit a one-line quote or a forty-line one.
fields.feature_2:
Drafts filled from your own data

Pull values from a submitted form or any tool with an API, HubSpot deals included. A value missing at the source stops the draft, and the app names the field that came back empty.
fields.feature_3:
AI reading for PDFs and scans

Read a policy number or an expiry date straight from an uploaded file into a named field. Any field the model is unsure of waits for a person to confirm it before the next step runs.
fields.feature_4:
Checks against your thresholds

Set the rules each value must pass: a discount above 15% fails, as does a contract with no signature page. Failures go to the named reviewer in Slack or email, file attached.
fields.feature_5:
A table row for every document

Write each drafted or received document to a database you own, with the record it came from and who reviewed it. Find a file by client or vendor instead of searching drives.
fields.feature_6:
Code you can take anywhere

Export the templates and the rules behind them to your GitHub on paid plans, along with the database. Keep changing them by prompting, or hand the code to any developer to extend.

fields.tab_content_1:
Turn a client questionnaire into an engagement letter draft

Every answer in Calder Law's intake form fills a field in the engagement letter, such as the matter type and the fee basis. Because this matter is litigation, the draft adds the $5,000 retainer clause. Ana Ruiz, the responsible attorney, can edit any clause before approving it, and only the approved version goes out.
fields.tab_content_2:
A priced quote the moment a deal reaches Proposal

When the Acme renewal moves to the Proposal stage in HubSpot, its line items are copied into the quote template. That quote, Q-2291, comes to $28,400. Any quote over $25,000 waits for Dev Patel, the sales director, before the rep can send it.
fields.tab_content_3:
Catch an underinsured vendor before the job starts

Vendors upload insurance certificates to Northwind Properties, and the app reads the policy number, expiry date and per-occurrence limit. Ridgeline Roofing's certificate lists $500,000 per occurrence, under its contract's $1,000,000 minimum. The vendor is asked for a new one, and the job stays on hold until one passes.
fields.tab_content_4:
Offer letters that go out once the hiring manager signs off

Moving a candidate to Offer in Lumen Studio's hiring tracker fills the offer letter template from the hiring record. Sam Okafor's letter carries a $96,000 base salary and goes to Mei Chen, the hiring manager, for approval. Sam then signs from a link on a phone.

fields.howto_description: Keep last month's files open while you work through these. Each step settles one decision the app needs, and the last one tests those decisions on real requests.
fields.howto_step_4_title: 04 Decide how incoming files are read
fields.howto_step_1_des: Collect ten recent copies of each document your team sends or receives every week. Mark which parts change and which never do, and note where the changing data lives today. A file with a stable structure and different names and amounts each time is the right place to start.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Take the latest version your lawyers or managers signed off on and replace each changing value with a named field. Keep their wording exactly as it is. Any clause that appears only sometimes gets its own field for now; the next step decides when it appears.
fields.howto_step_3_des: For every optional clause, write the condition that adds it: a multi-year deal gets a price escalator, and a remote hire gets the equipment policy. Plain sentences are enough. A rule nobody can explain to a new hire needs rewriting before it reaches the template.
fields.howto_step_4_des: List the documents people send you and the fields you need from each one. Name the check that matters most for each one, then mark the fields a person must always confirm. A supplier's changed bank account belongs on that list every time.
fields.howto_step_5_des: Not every draft needs a human, and some always do. Draw the line in one sentence per document: every letter to a new client gets a reviewer, and a renewal at last year's price does not. Name a second reviewer as well, for the weeks the first one is away.
fields.howto_step_6_title: 06 Choose where finished files are stored
fields.howto_step_6_des: Signed and approved PDFs can go to Google Drive, back to the CRM record, or into the app's own database. Pick one home per document type. Decide too whether rejected drafts are kept beside the approved ones or deleted.
fields.howto_step_7_title: 07 Run a week of real requests
fields.howto_step_7_des: Turn on one document type for one team and let real requests through for a week. Compare every draft with what the team would have written by hand. Adjust the template or the rules by prompting, then add the next document type once the first runs clean.

plan.angle: The top 10 splits document automation into two jobs: assembling documents from templates and rules (Wikipedia, Gavel, Conga, Checkbox) and reading incoming documents into data (Automation Anywhere, Microsoft AI Builder, Conexiom). Each vendor sells one half. This page wins by treating both as one pipeline an operator owns: intake answers and CRM data in, letters and quotes out, uploaded PDFs read into fields and checked against a rule, with every document and decision saved as a row. Real documents named (engagement letter, quote, certificate of insurance, offer letter) and an honest note on where Zapier, Make and n8n fit.

scope.evidence: H1 'Build Document Automation for What You Send and Receive' and meta description 'drafts quotes and letters and reads PDFs' cover both halves (generation and processing); no sibling primary (approval workflow, compliance automation) in a heading.

intent.evidence: PAA 'What does document automation mean?', 'What are some examples of document automation?' and 'What is the best document automation software?' all answered (FAQ 1, 3, 4); legal document automation (Gavel, NetDocuments in the top 10) covered by FAQ 5 and tab 1; processing vs generation split (Automation Anywhere, AI Builder) by FAQ 7; how-to in 7 steps.

specificity.evidence: Real documents and thresholds: 'the $5,000 retainer clause', 'quote, Q-2291, comes to $28,400. Any quote over $25,000 waits for Dev Patel', '$500,000 per occurrence, under its contract's $1,000,000 minimum', 'A supplier's changed bank account belongs on that list every time.'

openers.evidence: Paragraphs open on full sentences: 'Every answer in Calder Law's intake form fills a field...', 'When the Acme renewal moves to the Proposal stage in HubSpot...', 'Collect ten recent copies of each document...'.

craft.evidence: QC Q2/Q5/Q6/Q7 clean; FAQ answers lead with the answer ('No. Document processing automation takes files in...'); numeral slips are notes.

voice.evidence: Reads operator-written: 'Keep their wording exactly as it is.', 'A rule nobody can explain to a new hire needs rewriting before it reaches the template.', 'twenty invoices saved as one PDF leave the app guessing where each one ends'. No AI-tell vocabulary.

truth.evidence: faq item 8: 'if it highlights, the file was exported from Word or an accounting tool and the text comes out as typed. If nothing highlights, you are holding a scan.' A scan run through OCR (searchable PDF) also highlights, so the test is false for a common case. Everything else checks: claims_used approved; ABA Model Rule 1.5(b), AI Builder toolkit, Gavel, HubSpot quotes, Zapier template action, KPMG intelligent document automation all in domain_sources.

distinct.evidence: Four distinct documents (engagement letter, sales quote, certificate of insurance, offer letter); approval topics link out to 'approval workflow', 'contract approval workflow' and 'document approval workflow' rather than answering them; QC D2 clean.

faq.evidence: 10 on-topic questions from PAA, secondaries and the related search 'Document automation pdf'; hub link only in item 2; 3 sibling links; each answers in sentence 1 ('Yes, but check which kind of PDF you have first.').

findings.quote: Try to select a line of text: if it highlights, the file was exported from Word or an accounting tool and the text comes out as typed. If nothing highlights, you are holding a scan.
findings.issue: False as stated: a scanned page run through OCR (searchable PDF, the default on most office scanners and phone scanning apps) also highlights, so the test misreads a scan as a native export, and its text does not come out 'as typed'. No domain source covers the test. Only instance on the page (searched every field, image brief and chip prompts for highlight/scan/typed).
findings.fix: Drop the highlight test and state only what is true by definition, e.g. 'Yes. A PDF exported from Word or an accounting tool carries its text, so values come out exactly as typed. A scan is a picture of the page and is read with OCR, which can misread a character. Where senders can export the original file, ask them for that.' (domain_sources is at the 8-source cap, so avoid any claim that would need a new source).
